title: Cloud storage theft
overview: Review repeated bulk reads of restricted cloud objects by a principal outside its usual workload.
prerequisites: Know the basics of Cloud auditing and how to review authorization context.

attack.name: Data from Cloud Storage
attack.rationale: T1530 describes collection from cloud storage. External transfer requires additional evidence.

hypothesis: Repeated high-volume GetObject activity on restricted data by one identity warrants verifying purpose and destination.
evidence: Check the principal, data classification, object count and bucket. Compare workload history and transfer logs.
false_positive: An approved backup, restore or analytics load can read numerous restricted objects.
tuning: Separate scheduled jobs by role and baseline expected data volume per role and bucket.
response: Confirm scope and destination, preserve object access logs and restrict unauthorized sessions or roles.
prevention: Enable object-level audit for restricted storage, scope access and enforce approved destinations.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: The fixture contains read summaries. The records do not establish where data went after retrieval.

questions.prompt: What telemetry closes the destination question?
options: Transfer, egress or provider delivery records
questions.explanation: Successful reads establish access. Subsequent transfer evidence clarifies export.
Expected workload varies by bucket and role.
